newsitem.title: BOSNIA: UN starts training Serb mine disposal experts.
newsitem.headline: UN starts training Serb mine disposal experts.

text.p: The United Nations began training a group of 40 mine disposal experts in the Bosnian town of Banja Luka on Tuesday as part of a project organised by the U.N. Mine Action Centre.

The specialists will join a larger team to defuse about 1.5 million mines and other explosive devices believed to have been strewn across the Bosnian Serb Republic and between it and the Moslem-Croat Federation during the 1992-1995 war.
U.N. officials believe there are about three million mines scattered across 300 square kilometers.
The scheme is financed by the World Bank and the European Union. The training will last two months and is headed by U.N. mine expert Patrick Franc Gericke.
Since the signing of the Dayton peace agreement for Bosnia, 500 people have been killed by mines or other explosive devices on the territory of the Bosnian Serb Republic.
In Petrovo on Mount Ozren alone, 12 children have been killed by mines since peace was signed in December 1995.
Sreda Vucanovic, a Bosnian Serb government representative, said the job of mine removal in the Bosnian Serb Republic would take at least 20 years.

The mine disposal team for the Bosnian Serb Republic, including drivers and logistics, is expected to number 500 people, with each mine expert paid 1,300 German marks each month, seven times the average wage in the Serb entity.
